clue.text: Limp young thing rejected by detectives

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the young animal's name is read backwards

parts.note: a calf is a young cow, a young thing on the farm
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the UK police detectives

explanation.surface: A feeble young creature is turned away by police investigators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns CALF into FLAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something floppy and lacking firmness.

clue.text: End of Scandinavian country, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: belonging to Finland is Finnish

explanation.surface: The conclusion of a Nordic nation, so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: Finland is usually counted as Nordic and loosely as Scandinavian.
explanation.definitionFit: To end something is to bring it to a close or conclusion.

clue.text: International links might weaken without one

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: arm means power or might, as in the long arm of the law
the Roman numeral for one is I
to ail is to be weak or sickly

explanation.surface: Global connections could fail if one is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' puts I inside ARM, giving AIRM; then AIL follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters flown abroad by air connect people in different countries.

clue.text: Opera act rewritten to include long famous beauty

indicators.note: to include means to take in, so one piece goes inside the other
rewritten means composed afresh, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for long or large

explanation.surface: A section of an opera is revised to feature a celebrated beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rewritten' rearranges OPERAACT, and 'to include' places L among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian queen loved by Antony is famed for her beauty.

clue.text: Hell snares non-believer' we explain

indicators.note: snares means traps, so one piece is caught inside the other

parts.note: Dis is the Roman underworld, hence hell
an agnostic does not commit to belief in God

explanation.surface: The underworld traps a doubter, and we say why.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snares' puts AGNOSTIC inside DIS. The definition is loose: diagnostic work explains what is wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Diagnostic tests identify and account for a fault or illness.

clue.text: Agitated fluster won't be this!

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up, so the letters of the next word are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone in a flap is hardly going to be calm.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a flustered, agitated person is the opposite of calm and relaxed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in an agitated fluster is the opposite of being calm and relaxing.

clue.text: Blushing female gets away from lad

indicators.note: gets away from means leaves, so a letter is removed from the word

parts.note: Fred is a typical boy's name

explanation.surface: A woman goes pink as she escapes from a young man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets away from' removes F from FRED.
explanation.definitionFit: A blushing face turns crimson, the colour of embarrassment.

clue.text: American soldiers upset Greek character

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters read upwards

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: US troops overturn a figure from Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns AMGIS round.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the eighteenth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Fair old winds in US state

indicators.note: winds means twists, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Pleasant breezes of the past blow in an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winds' rearranges FAIROLD.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the southeastern state known as the Sunshine State.

clue.text: Endless mess on board ship, one hears

indicators.note: on board means carried within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a liner is an ocean-going passenger ship

indicators.note: endless means without its last letter

parts.note: a stew is a muddle or mess

explanation.surface: A sailor's untidy galley on a ship, with someone eavesdropping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' turns STEW into STE; 'on board' places STE inside LINER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone attending to sound is an auditor, a person who hears.

clue.text: Arranged us a minder (a child-minder)

indicators.note: arranged means set in a new order, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has organised a babysitter for the speaker and others.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman employed to look after young children is a nanny or child-minder.

clue.text: Obscene reversed part of dress or gown

indicators.note: reversed says the hidden letters are read backwards
part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something indecent has been turned inside out in a frock.
explanation.walkthrough: The run SSORG sits in 'dreSS OR Gown'; 'reversed' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Gross can mean vulgar, coarse or indecent, a synonym of obscene.

clue.text: Prove too much for exchange involving money

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: to exchange is to swap

explanation.surface: A financial trade overwhelms someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' puts M inside SWAP.
explanation.definitionFit: To be overwhelmed by work is to be swamped; something that proves too much for you overwhelms you.

clue.text: Product of tree in can, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Fruit from a tree might end up tinned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges TREEINCAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A peach-like fruit is something a tree produces, its product.

clue.text: Managing member of rock group, one in top position

parts.note: coping means managing
a member of the Rolling Stones is a Stone

explanation.surface: A rock band's manager, one at the top.
explanation.definitionFit: A capping slab laid along the top of a wall sits in the highest position.

clue.text: Battered, presumably, till all lumps removed?

definitions.text: Battered, presumably, till all lumps removed?

parts.words: Battered, presumably, till all lumps removed?
parts.note: read as kitchen talk, batter is whisked smooth and then cooked into a thin flat disc; read as a phrase it means utterly level

explanation.surface: Something beaten until no bumps are left.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something completely level, likened to a thin fried batter disc.

clue.text: Cancelled nude dancing, if unwell, upset internally

indicators.note: internally means inside, so one piece goes within the other
dancing means moving about, so the letters of these words are jumbled
upset in a down clue means turned over, so the letters read upwards

parts.note: ill means unwell

explanation.surface: Naked dancing was called off as the performer felt sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges NUDEIF to NUFIED; 'upset' turns ILL into LLI; 'internally' places LLI inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To render void or invalid is to cancel.

clue.text: Valued encounters in river, heading north

indicators.note: heading north in a down clue means read upwards
in means placed inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
meets means encounters

explanation.surface: Precious meetings by a river as one travels north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places MEETS inside DEE, giving DEMEETSE; 'heading north' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: Highly regarded and respected things are prized, valued.

clue.text: Lover of spectacle? Fallen saint is last one

indicators.note: fallen suggests something collapsed and jumbled, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A saint who has sinned ends up at the back of the queue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fallen' rearranges SAINTISLASTONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who loves sensation and drama, playing things up for effect, is a lover of spectacle.

clue.text: Composer, one otherwise engaged in notes?

indicators.note: engaged in means held within, so the pieces go inside the others

parts.note: N is an abbreviation for note, so two notes give two Ns
the Roman numeral for one is I
else means otherwise

explanation.surface: A musician writing, one busy with other pieces of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaged in' places IELSE between N and N. Carl Nielsen was a Danish composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Nielsen was a Danish symphonist.

clue.text: Jazzy carpets — they have many colours

indicators.note: jazzy means lively and freewheeling, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Bright rugs are multicoloured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jazzy' rearranges CARPETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Bands of light split by a prism show the full range of hues.

clue.text: Writer penning western epic? On the contrary

indicators.note: this word says the answer sits inside the words it governs, as a run of their own consecutive letters
the clue says the writer pens the words, but on the contrary the words pen, or enclose, the writer

explanation.surface: An author writes a cowboy saga, or rather the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is inside 'weSTERN Epic'. Laurence Sterne wrote Tristram Shandy.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Sterne was an eighteenth-century novelist.

clue.text: Soccer team sees no end of trouble -time for a break

parts.note: a football side has eleven players

indicators.note: no here means without, so a letter is removed from the word before
end of picks the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A football side sees no end of trouble before half-time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end of trouble' removes E, the last letter of 'trouble', from SEES, leaving SES. Elevenses is a British mid-morning snack break.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a short mid-morning break for tea and a snack is called by this name.

clue.text: Sounds like limitations on magic show host

indicators.note: sounds like signals that the letters are spoken aloud

parts.note: the limits of the word magic are its first and last letters, M and C

explanation.surface: Restrictions on a conjuror's act, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: The first and last letters of 'magic' are M and C, said as two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A master of ceremonies presents and compères a show.

clue.text: That is it, surrounding most of work-table

indicators.note: surrounding means placed around, so one piece goes outside the other

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: most of means all but the last letter

parts.note: a desk is a table to work at

explanation.surface: Someone declares that's it, around most of their workbench.
explanation.walkthrough: DESK loses K to 'most of', giving DES, which IT surrounds.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase, shortened to i.e., is used to mean 'that is to say'.

clue.text: 22 enthralling us, one offering songs etc

indicators.note: enthralling means captivating and holding, so other letters go inside

parts.note: the answer to 22 down is a show host, abbreviated MC
taken as written
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A compere captivating an audience with songs and more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enthralling' places US and I inside MC.
explanation.definitionFit: Songs and other compositions are examples of musical works.

clue.text: Singer is tense during boring work, right?

indicators.note: during means within, so one piece is set inside the other

parts.note: a chore is a tedious task
taken as written
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A vocalist feels strained during a dull job, is that right?
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' places IST inside CHORE, then R follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a choir is someone who sings.

clue.text: Has the power to preserve

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means is able to, and also means to seal food in tins to keep it.

clue.text: University boss enthrals worker, describing some Italian poetry

indicators.note: enthrals means holds captive, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a dean heads a university faculty
the ant is the crossword's usual worker insect

explanation.surface: A head of faculty captivates an employee by talking about Italian verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enthrals' places ANT inside DEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective refers to the work of the poet of the Divine Comedy.

clue.text: Foreplay to mating?

parts.note: read as chess, the final phase of play leads up to checkmate

explanation.surface: A coy question about the prelude to sex.
explanation.definitionFit: The last stage of a chess game is the play that leads up to checkmate.
